title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement: Given an unsorted list `nums` of integers, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive values (order in `nums` does not matter). Duplicates do not extend the sequence. An empty list has length 0.

predict_steps.prompt: Why start a run only at 1, not at 2, for nums containing 1,2,3,4?
predict_steps.answer: 1 has no predecessor 0 in the set
predict_steps.hint: Starts are values where x-1 is absent.

predict_steps.prompt: From start 1, how long is the consecutive run in the demo?

viva.question: Why can a hash set beat sorting when measuring the longest consecutive run?
expected_points: membership tests are amortized constant time
you only start a run at a value whose predecessor is missing
expected total work is linear in the number of distinct values
sorting would pay an n log n tax just to walk adjacent numbers

viva.question: What breaks if duplicates remain in the working set?
expected_points: a set collapses duplicates so length counts distinct values
repeats must not inflate a consecutive run
starting a run twice on the same value would overcount work
the statement cares about values, not index multiplicity

viva.question: Why expand a streak only when num-1 is absent?
expected_points: that condition marks the unique start of a consecutive run
middle values are skipped so each run is counted once
amortized work stays linear because each value expands at most once
starting inside a run would recount the same chain
